span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An intention instantiates a task-set that pre-tunes the automatic perceptual-classification-response chain, so masked primes are run through the same task-defined categorization as targets and interfere at the response stage
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Above-chance prime discrimination arises because forced-choice responding under uncertainty recruits the very same practised automatic classification processes, not because the primes were consciously seen
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **IT ARGUES IN 2007 WHAT hesselmann2016 OFFERS IN 2016 AS SPECULATION:** `Quotation withheld. WE CHALLENGE THIS VIEW by arguing that some automatic processes may indeed BE UNDER INTENTIONAL CONTROL.` hesselmann2016 (Q-818) closes with `SPECULATIVELY, the category task might have DESENSITIZED perceptual pathways ... the shape task SENSITIZED` them, citing Kiefer 2012. **This paper made it the thesis of three experiments nine years earlier, and the 2016 paper does not cite it.** Two records, one claim, nine years, no link - the corpus can show that without asserting anyone should have known
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE AWARENESS RESULT CUTS ACROSS Finkbeiner2011 FROM THE OTHER SIDE:** `Quotation withheld.` **The same primes are above chance under one awareness test and at chance under another.** Finkbeiner2011 (Q-810) argues the prime-classification task UNDERESTIMATES awareness because it is harder; this shows the answer depends on WHICH TASK, not only how hard. **Every subliminal claim in this corpus rests on a single such test**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND ONE SENTENCE MAKES THE WHOLE FRAMING AWKWARD:** `priming was AS PRONOUNCED when the primes were VISIBLE as when they were INVISIBLE.` **If visibility does not change the effect, awareness was never the variable.** Schmidt2010 (Q-812) reaches the same place from a different paradigm - a qualitative dissociation with the stimuli in plain view - and this is the second record today to arrive there. Two papers, two methods, one conclusion the masked-priming literature is organised against
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE MECHANISM IS THE TASK, NOT THE STIMULUS:** `Quotation withheld.` Same words, same masks, same subjects - **only the instruction changed, and the priming changed with it.** That is a manipulation of the observer rather than of the stimulus, which is rare in this corpus and is why the result bears on what `automatic` can mean
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: automatic —distinct-from→ intentional control
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE ENTAILMENT THE PAPER BREAKS, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST THING IN THE RECORD.** The field treats `automatic` as implying `not under intentional control`; Eckstein and Perrig argue `some automatic processes may indeed be under intentional control`. So the two properties come apart, and `distinct-from` says exactly that. Weight 0.95: both terms are in the quote and the separation is the article's whole contribution.

span.label: With one and the same word set, masked priming appeared only on the dimension the current task required: valence congruency affected only the valence task and animacy congruency only the animacy task.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A brand-new, never-practised classification (a disjunction/conjunction of the two practised categories) produced larger task-relevant priming than the simple single-dimension tasks did.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Although participants said they saw nothing of the primes, they classified the primes above chance whenever the direct test used the same semantic task they had practised on targets.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When prime awareness was probed with a lexical decision task instead, the same masked primes could not be discriminated at all, inverting the usual ordering of word-processing stages.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Making the primes visible by removing the masks did not abolish priming, so the interference could not be consciously filtered out.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Amount of priming was unrelated to how well an individual could discriminate the primes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Task-specific priming was not a by-product of practice accumulating during the test itself, since priming did not grow from the first to the second half of testing.
